items.title: Keter Betts interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 11, 1996
items.q: The young piano player was Wynton Kelly. ... Think of in your lifetime, just in the short amount of time you’re working with Wynton Kelly

ctx.x: He was doing rhythm & blues, so you got a new —

I think the reason that I did that was the fact that I was going to get a chance to travel and see the country. You know, after studying geography, which you don’t have in the schools now anymore, but after studying geography I said well I’ll get a chance to see the country, it’ll be a new experience, and it was. And at that time there was hardly no, you know like no freeways, there was none. In fact the only thing that you had was save for like the Merrick Parkway, there were a few of those around the country.…
Boy, talk about starting on the top. Did you ever have any trouble with that particular group like traveling in different parts of the country?
